transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I'd like to get started on reviewing the medication-safety simulation assessment plan. As I understand it, we have 12 students who need to complete this assessment this term, and the draft plan currently calls for a faculty evaluator, two rotations of six students, an assessment date of May 8, 2027, and a results-entry date of June 21, 2027. Before I give my final approval, I'd like to go through our normal review routine with all of you — the clinical coordinator, simulation-lab manager, registrar, and student-services coordinator. Let's start by hearing any initial thoughts or concerns about the draft plan.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a compliance concern with the draft plan. During this month's clinical-compliance review, I confirmed that the state nursing board's current medication-simulation rule requires the evaluator to be a current, unencumbered registered nurse. However, the draft plan only specifies 'faculty evaluator' without stating this RN requirement. We should update the language to explicitly require a current, unencumbered RN before Dr. Morgan grants final approval.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to raise an equipment and safety concern with the draft plan. I completed the equipment check yesterday, and only three of our medication pumps have current calibration certificates. Our lab's safety procedure limits each pump rotation to three students. With only three calibrated pumps available, the current plan of two rotations of six students would exceed the safety limit of three students per pump rotation. We need to revise the rotation count — likely to four rotations of three students each — before the plan can be approved.
